purpose: This medication is used to treat Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in patients 6 years and older. It helps improve focus, attention, and control impulsive behaviors. It is typically used as part of a broader treatment plan that may include therapy and other support.
how_it_works: This medicine has two active parts that work together to help your brain stay focused throughout the day. One part works quickly to give you an early boost in concentration, while the other part is released slowly over time to keep you focused for longer. Together, they help balance certain chemicals in your brain, like dopamine and norepinephrine, that are involved in attention and self-control.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include decreased appetite, trouble sleeping, upset stomach, nausea, feeling irritable or moody, dry mouth, increased heart rate, and headache. Many of these may improve as your body gets used to the medication.
warnings: This medication has a risk of abuse and dependence, so it is important to take it exactly as prescribed and not share it with others. It can raise blood pressure and heart rate, so let your doctor know if you have any heart problems. It is not safe to take with certain antidepressants called MAOIs. Tell your doctor if you have a history of anxiety, seizures, or mental health conditions. Avoid taking it late in the day as it can cause difficulty sleeping.
typical_dosing: For most patients 6 and older, the starting dose is one capsule (39.2 mg/7.8 mg) taken by mouth once every morning. Your doctor may adjust the dose based on how you respond to it, up to a maximum of two capsules per day. It can be taken with or without food, and the capsule can be swallowed whole or opened and sprinkled on food if needed.
